sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Box, header, title and description
sections.what: Draws the rounded bordered box, the top header area, the bold title and the grey description text.
sections.why: Keeps the main pieces of a card consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: The title is a plain box rather than a heading, so it is not announced as one.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Body, footer and exports
sections.what: Draws the main content area with its top padding removed so it sits right under the header, plus a footer row for buttons or notes. Then it makes all parts available to other files.
sections.why: Lets the body sit close to the header while keeping the outer padding.
sections.watch_out: The footer is a single row, so many long buttons can overflow on narrow screens.

summary: A set of plain bordered boxes for grouping content, with a header, title, description, body and footer.
purpose: Groups related information visually on a page, such as a summary panel.
why: Likely reason: a shared card layout reused across pages. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Builds the bordered box. Step 2: Builds the header, title and description. Step 3: Builds the body and footer. Step 4: Makes all six parts available to other files.
inputs: Content placed inside each part, plus optional extra style classes or attributes.
outputs: A rounded, bordered box with padded sections on screen.
risks: The title is drawn as a plain box rather than a heading, so screen readers and the page outline miss it. Padding is fixed, so custom spacing needs the page to override it.
debug: If spacing looks wrong, check the extra classes on the parts. If the title is missing from the page outline, have the page render the title as a heading.
